deep.reconstruction:
Context: these are lecture notes (Riemann's own draft or an auditor's notes) for a course on functions of a complex variable. The previous page treats ∫X dx + Y dy, Green's theorem and ∫f(z)dz. This page opens the next hour: "In the last hour we dealt with the short investigation of expanding a function in a power series and various associated laws. First, about the convergence of a given power series."

(1) Object. The power series S(z) = a_0 + a_1 z + a_2 z^2 + ... + a_n z^n + ... .

(2) Comparison series. The geometric series 1 + a + a^2 + ... + a^n has sum (1 - a^{n+1})/(1 - a). The page writes '+ a^n' under the series and then this quotient. Hence (stated): a geometric series diverges if a > 1 and converges if a < 1, with a ≥ 0. There is a fragmentary definition: 'Eine Reihe heißt convergent ...'.

(3) Comparison principle (the marginal fragment). 'If a series all of whose terms are positive converges ...' The implied completion is mine: a series whose terms are bounded in modulus by the terms of a convergent positive series converges absolutely.

(4) Convergence part. Suppose that for all sufficiently large n, mod(a_n z^n) < a^n with a fixed a < 1. The page writes 'a ≦ 1', which should be strict. Then S(z) converges absolutely by comparison with the geometric series. The condition is equivalent to (mod a_n)^{1/n} · |z| < a < 1 for large n; the line '(mod a_n)^{1/n} [struck symbol] < a < 1' encodes this, the struck symbol presumably being the modulus of z.

(5) Definition of the critical quantity. Put f(m) = sup_{n>m} (mod a_n)^{1/n}. Then (mod a_n)^{1/n} ≤ f(m) for n > m. The function f is non-increasing in m, so it has a limit f(∞) = δ. In modern terms δ = limsup_{n→∞} |a_n|^{1/n}.

(6) Divergence part. Take |z| = r > 1/δ. Since f is non-increasing with limit δ, f(m) ≥ δ for all m, hence f(m)·r ≥ rδ > 1. The page then writes mod(a_n z^n) ≥ (rδ)^n and, in the last line, a comparison of mod a_n z^n with rδ.

The correct argument (my completion): because sup_{n>m} |a_n|^{1/n}·r > 1 for every m, for every m there is some n > m with |a_n|^{1/n} r > 1, i.e. |a_n z^n| > 1. So the terms do not tend to 0 and the series diverges.

Conversely (implicit, mine): for r < 1/δ choose a with rδ < a < 1. Then for large m, f(m)·r < a, so |a_n z^n| < a^n for n > m, and step (4) gives convergence.

Conclusion (implicit): the series converges absolutely for |z| < 1/δ and diverges for |z| > 1/δ. This is the Cauchy–Hadamard radius of convergence R = 1/limsup |a_n|^{1/n}.
errors: 'a ≦ 1' in the comparison mod(a_n z^n) < a^n must be strict (a < 1); with a = 1 the comparison series 1+1+1+... diverges and nothing follows.

'mod(a_n z^n) ≥ (rδ)^n' is not justified as written. f(m) ≥ δ is a statement about suprema of tails; individual terms |a_n|^{1/n} may all lie strictly below δ (limsup approached from below), so |a_n|^{1/n} ≥ δ need not hold for any n. The correct statement: since sup_{n>m}|a_n|^{1/n}·r > 1, infinitely many n satisfy |a_n z^n| > 1.

The final line (mod a_n z^n compared with rδ, transcribed as ≤) is garbled. What is needed is |a_n z^n| > 1 for infinitely many n (terms not tending to zero). Neither '≤ rδ' nor '≥ rδ' is the right inequality for the conclusion.
The case δ = 0 (r > 1/δ meaningless, R = ∞) and δ = ∞ (R = 0) are not addressed; this is typical for lecture notes, not a real error.

results.what: Finite geometric sum 1 + a + ... + a^n = (1 - a^{n+1})/(1 - a); geometric series converges for a < 1, diverges for a > 1
Comparison test: termwise domination by a convergent positive series implies (absolute) convergence
results.modern_name: comparison test / absolute convergence via majorant

results.what: Definition δ = lim_{m→∞} sup_{n>m} |a_n|^{1/n} via a non-increasing function f(m); convergence for |z| < 1/δ and divergence for |z| > 1/δ
results.modern_name: Cauchy–Hadamard formula for the radius of convergence (root test with limsup)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy 1821 ('la plus grande des limites'); rediscovered and popularized by Hadamard 1888 (thesis 1892)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard lecture treatment of power-series convergence via the root test with a limsup, already in Cauchy (1821). Riemann's lectures on complex function theory, which treat power series convergence, are known through auditors' notes and have been studied (e.g. by Neuenschwander). The explicit construction of the limsup as the limit of the non-increasing tail suprema f(m) is a slightly careful touch for c. 1850s–60s, but not new. Hence the result is only mildly notable as a detail of his teaching.

checkable.asserts: finite geometric sum formula used on the page
for a_n = 2^n, δ = 2, so the radius of convergence is 1/δ = 1/2 (example of the criterion)
for a_n = n, δ = 1, radius 1: polynomial factors do not change the radius
for a_n = 1/n!, δ = 0, so the series (exp) converges for all z (case δ = 0 not treated on the page)
|a_n z^n| = a^n with a = 5/6 < 1 gives convergence (comparison with geometric series)

transcription_corrections: Under the series the image shows '+ a^n' as part of the comparison geometric series 1 + a + ... + a^n; it is not a separate formula.
The comparison line reads 'mod(a_n z^n) < a^n   a ≦ 1' (with ≦ as written, mathematically should be <).
In '(mod a_n)^{1/n} ✗ < a < 1' there is a struck-out symbol after the root (likely |z| or r), so the intended line is (mod a_n)^{1/n}·|z| < a < 1.
'f(∞) = δ' is written to the right of '(mod a_n)^{1/n} ≦ f(m), n > m' on the same line.
The last line's relation sign is ambiguous in the image (reads as '≦' or '≧' rδ); it is not certainly '≤'.
Opening sentence: 'verschiedene dazugehörige Gesetze' is uncertain; the image is consistent with a different adjective (e.g. 'verschiedenartige'); the sense ('various associated laws') is unaffected.
Marginal note: 'Wenn eine Reihe, in denen alle Glieder positiv sind, convergirt' — the image reads 'positiv' (or 'gleichartig'?) followed by 'convergirt'; the sentence is unfinished.
